result:
I ran all four materials, but machine data was the weak point. Cork autoclave expansion and cutting have no rows at all, because I couldn't find datasheets with power, throughput and mass. No material hit a STOP.

Values are GWP-fossil A1–A3 per kg (EF 3.1), compared against the latest ÖKOBAUDAT release (OBD_2024_III, 13 Nov 2026).

| Material | Route kept | Ours | ÖKOBAUDAT median | Result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| sawn_softwood | exact match (kiln-dried softwood market) | 0.146 | 0.209 (6 EPDs) | CHECK 1 pass |
| cork | approximate match (cork slab market), flagged | 0.959 | 0.512 (1 EPD) | CHECK 2 and CHECK 3 fail, so it went to REVIEW |
| fibre_cement | approximate match (large-format facing tile, GLO market) | 1.39 | 1.08 (7 EPDs) | CHECK 2 pass |
| stone_wool | built from scratch | 1.35 | 1.19 (4 EPDs) | CHECK 3 pass |

- **Cork:** the built LCI came out at 0.0355 kg/kg because it is missing the autoclave and cutting steps. In REVIEW the approximate match was only slightly closer to the median (distance 0.871 vs 0.931). A complete build would probably be higher and might pass.
- **Machine steps:** grinding for cork is the only step where I could compare three manufacturers. Their datasheets give ranges per series, so I used midpoints.
- **Stone wool:** with no machine data for cupola melting, fiberising, curing oven and cutting, I took energy from EU BREF Table 3.29 and wrote no machine rows. All heat is booked as natural gas, although a cupola burns coke. Three constituents (briquettes, binder, oil) are proxies. The input shares sum to 0.997, not 1.
- **Release mismatch:** the workbook's ÖKOBAUDAT links for sawn softwood, fibre cement and stone wool point to older dataset versions. I used the latest release through the ÖKOBAUDAT API, read-only.
- **Median set:** the protocol doesn't define "the product's category" for the median. I used product-matching subsets; the alternatives are in `epd_check.csv`, and none changed a pass or fail.

`protocol_issues.md` lists 30 ambiguities. The main ones are the D1 tolerance, market vs production for fibre cement, RoW ranking before Portugal for raw cork, and how to handle unresolved machine steps. I also installed `pypdf` in `/tmp/pylib` to read downloaded PDFs; nothing else was written outside `runs/batch_1/`.

Everything is in `runs/batch_1/`; the scripts that produced it are in `work/`:
- `summary.md`
- `protocol_issues.md`
- `decisions.csv`
